priorFindingsVerification.note: Cross-checked ledger.js:20-24 (appendChild is a plain fs.appendFileSync with no internal try/catch, confirmed can throw) and lock.mjs:187-209 (withGigLock's finally block releases the lock via fs.unlink on ANY exception thrown out of fn(), regardless of which line inside fn() threw). The revised spec text (behavioral-spec.md lines 765-827) correctly re-grounds the reconciliation trigger on LEDGER STATE alone (an unterminated 'provisioning'/'disbursement_uncertain' row for the lender's own highest n) rather than lock staleness, uniformly covering: (a) crash, (b) in-process payViaFacilitator exception, and (c) the follow-up appendChild call itself throwing -- the exact third terminal state the finding identified. It ALSO now specifies the second sub-gap (reconciliation lookup itself throwing): the attempt fails cleanly, zero row appended, zero sequence number consumed, lock released normally, safely retriable (lines 814-827). New Tier-2 proof obligations PROP-106k/PROP-106l (verification-architecture.md lines 130-131) back both cases with concrete fixtures. No remaining gap found.

'Logged,' precisely defined (behavioral-spec.md lines 1302-1319): a rejected replay (same-loan OR cross-loan) is recorded EXCLUSIVELY via an out-of-band mechanism, and THE SYSTEM SHALL NEVER append a new loans.jsonl row for it -- a binding SHALL with explicit rationale tied to the last-write-wins convention every other reduction in this spec depends on. Backed by a Tier-0 structural check (verification-architecture.md line ~139, PROP-108e: 'a structural/Tier-0 read of verifyRepayment's own replay-rejection branch confirming it never calls appendChild'). The finding's secondary point (no canonical row-schema table / no explicit discriminator between a disbursement-side txHash and a repayment-side txHash) is also substantively addressed: the replay-blocklist is now explicitly scoped to 'the set of every txHash ALREADY recorded on a previously-verified, credited REPAYMENT row (every row this feature itself appended after a PRIOR successful verifyRepayment call)' (lines 1286-1289) -- distinguishing by APPEND-SOURCE rather than by an explicit schema field, which is sufficient to close the security-relevant ambiguity (whether a loan's own disbursement txHash could be misread as an already-credited repayment and block a legitimate first repayment).

New Tier-0 proof obligation PROP-105h (verification-architecture.md lines 120, 154-156) now explicitly requires a control-flow read of the REAL, PRODUCTION REQ-106 issuance code -- not PROP-105g's mocked-caller fixture -- confirming it imports and calls evaluateColdStartKillSwitch BEFORE acquiring the loan_${lenderId} lock. Gate item (2) (verification-architecture.md lines 235-240) explicitly instructs the adversary that PROP-105g's mock is NOT sufficient evidence and that PROP-105h's real-code read is required. The 'a computed flag nobody checks' gap is closed at the verification-obligation level.

evidence.description: REQ-102's own stated invariant ('at most one outstanding loan at a time') is not actually enforced across different lenders -- REQ-106's per-lender lock (loan_${lenderId}) provides zero serialization for a borrower being evaluated concurrently, or across an unbounded reconciliation-delay window, by two DIFFERENT lenders

REQ-106's own Edge Cases explicitly frame cross-lender non-contention as 'intentional, not a bug' without ever acknowledging this defeats REQ-102's borrower-side single-in-flight invariant, the exact same class of gap (lock scope narrower than invariant scope) this spec has already hardened three times (FIND-103/FIND-201/FIND-301) for the lender side alone

No condition anywhere in REQ-101/102/105/111 requires lender_id !== borrower_id -- a self-funded citizen can self-loan-and-self-repay at negligible real cost to freely inflate successfulOnTimeRepayments, defeating REQ-105's core cold-start risk-mitigation rationale and corrupting computeColdStartRepaymentRate's own monitoring signal

issued_ms is used six times to drive REQ-109's default-detection clock and REQ-105's cold-start ordering but is never defined relative to REQ-106's own two distinct ledger-row timestamps (provisioned_ms vs. the follow-up active row), creating a real ambiguity in the crash-recovery/reconciliation-delay path this spec otherwise hardens carefully
PROP-102c is a static, non-concurrent fixture; it never exercises concurrent cross-lender evaluation of the SAME borrower

PROP-106e tests only loan_id collision-freedom across two different lenders -- it asserts nothing about whether the SAME borrower_id could appear as borrower on both concurrently-issued loans, so a fixture proving PROP-106e could still exhibit the FIND-401 double-loan bug undetected
Zero PROPs anywhere in the 149-line table require lender_id !== borrower_id, or specify issued_ms's set-point relative to REQ-106's two-phase provisional/active append
